topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes students to the final course lecture and outlines the learning objectives for cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain conventional cancer therapies that physically ablate or non-specifically damage dividing cells, including their clinical applications, toxicities, and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Tumor Vulnerabilities and Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that target intrinsic cancer cell defects, including hormone receptor dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failure, and DNA repair deficiencies via synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction and Kinase Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogenic driver kinases using small-molecule inhibitors, alongside the clinical challenges of acquired resistance, off-target effects, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe engineered antibody therapeutics designed to bind tumor-associated surface antigens, either to inhibit receptor signaling and trigger immune responses or to deliver cytotoxic drugs directly to cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the immune system's role in cancer control and detail therapeutic approaches that activate or engineer T cells to destroy tumors, including checkpoint blockade, BiTEs, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Challenges, Clinical Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the systemic challenges of tumor heterogeneity and resistance, assess historical survival trends, and explore future clinical and ethical perspectives in cancer treatment.
